claim.why_it_matters: The printed subsection heading is a plain paragraph in the markdown (compare '### 3.1 SYNTAX RULES' on page 149 and '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings' on page 151); the outline loses clause IV.4.1.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-4 (PDF p150, rendered at 300 dpi) shows '4.1 CHARACTER SET' as a plain unmarked heading line, set the same way as '4.2 LANGUAGE STRUCTURE' and '4.2.1 Separators' on the same page. page-150.md carries the identical text '4.1 CHARACTER SET' on its own line in the same position, followed by every body paragraph. The claim's own pdf_says and markdown_says are identical. The only difference is the absence of markdown '#' heading markup, which is formatting, not content: no words, numbers or clause text are missing or changed. The same plain-line treatment applies to 4.2 and 4.2.1 on this page, and the sibling verdicts verify-p148-2 and verify-p159-1 reject the same kind of claim for the same reason. A missing '#' affects navigation only and does not change the meaning of the standard.
